subject: truck2077
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: futuristic militarized truck from 2077.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk, extremely intricate.
reasoning:
I'm planning a moderately sized TypeScript module that builds a truck with a chassis joint root, wheel joints, and basic geometry/colors, plus a glow kit import, keeping the SDK usage safe and compact.

I'm working out proportions and placements for the chassis, wheels, cab, hood, and bed, along with picking a gunmetal and neon color palette and defining a box helper for constructing the body panels with rotation support.

Now I'm detailing the wheel assemblies with tires, rims, glowing neon rings, and bolts, then planning the roof turret, light bar, antenna, decal textures, headlights, grille, bumper spikes, and rear thrusters to flesh out the vehicle's combat-ready look.

Still writing part helper...

Working out cab dimensions now: a solid lower body section, a glass greenhouse above it with pillars, a roof trim box, and a raked windscreen plane angled forward to suggest a sloped front window.

Now moving to the hood and front end — building a sloped hood box with ridge details and glowing vent slits, plus a dark grille, glowing headlight boxes, and a front bumper. Then I'm laying out the truck bed: floor, side walls, tailgate, and a front wall, with plans to add a cargo rack or missile pod structure on top.

Working out the turret placement — deciding to mount it on a pedestal in the bed rather than the cab roof, raising it high enough that the barrel clears the cab's roofline while aiming forward, and adjusting the pedestal height and turret position until the geometry fits without clipping.

Now I'm adding missile pods outboard of the turret, a glowing light bar and antenna on the roof, and fender flares to cover the wheel arches without intersecting the body. I'm also setting up the chassis frame rails and making sure parts get assigned to the correct bone.

Rear thrusters will sit at the back as z-aligned cylinders with a glowing disc cap to suggest exhaust bells, which I'll code compactly.
